intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, traversing stunning alpine terrain between Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacial lakes, and ancient beech forests. A multi-day hike offering some of the most spectacular scenery in the Southern Hemisphere.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk this iconic 10km return trail through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, crossing swing bridges over glacial rivers with jaw-dropping views of New Zealand's highest peak. The trail ends at the stunning Hooker Glacier Lake filled with floating icebergs. A relatively accessible yet awe-inspiring alpine hike.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord surrounded by towering peaks and cascading waterfalls, then hike a section of the famous Milford Track through ancient rainforest. Spot dolphins, seals, and penguins in their natural habitat. A guided full-day experience combining two of Fiordland's best adventures.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Forest Hike
experiences.description: Soak in natural geothermal mineral pools surrounded by the Southern Alps, then explore the Hanmer Forest Park trails through fragrant pine forests with panoramic mountain views. The combination of restorative hot pools and scenic hiking makes this a perfect recovery day experience for active travellers.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

The trail ends at the stunning Hooker Glacier Lake filled with floating icebergs. A relatively accessible yet awe-inspiring alpine hike.

The combination of restorative hot pools and scenic hiking makes this a perfect recovery day experience for active travellers.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day - Flight LH lands at 13:00, no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, grab a local SIM card at the airport for budget navigation. Take the affordable Christchurch Metro Purple Line bus ($8 NZD) into the city centre. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a relaxed walk along the Beachfront promenade to get oriented and enjoy the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby beachfront area on foot. Stroll along the esplanade and watch the sunset over the water. Head to a local fish and chip shop for a classic New Zealand budget dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the plane or grab a muffin/coffee at the airport café (~$5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or grab a meal deal sandwich from a supermarket near the resort (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Classic Kiwi fish and chips from a local takeaway shop near the beachfront (~$12-15 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a free South Island map at the airport i-SITE visitor centre. Download the FreeWalks NZ app and AllTrails for free trail maps. Exchange currency or use ATM at the airport for best rates. Confirm resort check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and explore the coastal beachfront on foot. Walk the shoreline for a free morning stretch, taking in the fresh sea air and views. Visit a local farmers market or bakery for a cheap breakfast before heading out for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a local bus toward Hanmer Springs (approximately 1.5 hours from Christchurch area). Arrive and check out the Hanmer Forest Park trails — hike the Conical Hill Walk (2.5km, free entry) for panoramic views of the alpine basin and surrounding peaks. Pack a picnic lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: After the hike, treat yourself to a session at Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools. Evening entry rates are typically cheaper and the pools are magical under the darkening sky. Budget option: use the public pools rather than private pools (~$25-30 NZD). Return to resort.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread roll and coffee from a local bakery near the resort (~$6-8 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch — buy supplies from a supermarket (sandwiches, fruit, snacks ~$8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the resort kitchen using supermarket groceries (~$10-12 NZD) or grab a cheap burger from a local Hanmer Springs café (~$14 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools: book online in advance for discounts. Wear comfortable hiking shoes. Bring a towel and swimwear for the pools. Check opening hours for the thermal pools before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Port Hills area near Christchurch for a morning hike. The Crater Rim Walkway offers stunning views over the city and Lyttelton Harbour — completely free and accessible. Aim to start by 8:00am to avoid midday heat. The walk to Sugarloaf and back is about 6km.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive down to Lyttelton township (15 minutes from Port Hills). Explore the charming harbour village, browse the Saturday Farmers Market if timing aligns, or just wander the quirky main street. Visit the free Lyttelton Museum to learn about the region's history. Take the scenic road back to the resort along the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Cook dinner using groceries from a local supermarket to keep costs down. Spend the evening planning the upcoming multi-day road trip to Mount Cook, downloading offline maps and reading trail notes.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or cereal at the resort using grocery supplies (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap pie or sausage roll from a Lyttelton bakery (~$5-7 NZD)
meals.dinner: Home-cooked pasta or stir-fry at resort using supermarket ingredients (~$8-10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers for the Port Hills hike — morning winds can be cool even in November. Lyttelton has free street parking. Check if the resort has a communal kitchen for cooking. Stock up on groceries today for the next few days of road trip snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the scenic drive south toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3.5 hours). Stop at Lake Tekapo en route — arrive by 10:00am. Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd (free entry) on the lakeshore and photograph the stunning turquoise lake. Walk the short Mt John Summit Track or lakeside path for free views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Aoraki/Mount Cook Village (1 hour from Tekapo). Check in to the DOC campsite or YHA hostel for budget accommodation. Head straight to the Hooker Valley Track trailhead — begin this iconic 10km return hike through the national park, crossing swing bridges over glacial streams with dramatic views of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Hooker Valley Track by late afternoon (allow 3-4 hours total). Watch the alpenglow on Mount Cook at dusk from the village. Cook dinner at the hostel/campsite kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure — toast and eggs from grocery supplies (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Tekapo or on the trail — sandwiches and snacks from pre-bought groceries (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a hearty meal at the hostel kitchen — pasta with canned tomato sauce and vegetables (~$8-10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Book DOC campsite or YHA Mount Cook in advance — they fill quickly in November. The Hooker Valley Track is free and one of New Zealand's best short walks. Wear sturdy footwear and bring waterproof layers. Carry 2L of water per person on the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Rise at dawn for the Hooker Valley Track again or take the Kea Point Track (2 hours return, free) for views of the Mueller Glacier terminal lake and ice face. This is a slightly shorter alternative that complements yesterday's hike. The morning light on the glaciers is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre at The Hermitage (small entry fee ~$5 NZD or free to browse the foyer exhibits). Learn about the history of mountaineering in the park. Take the short Governors Bush Walk (1 hour loop, free) through native kāmahi forest near the village.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Twizel for a cheap dinner. Spend the night at a budget campsite or holiday park in Twizel (~$15-20 NZD per person).

meals.breakfast: Muesli and coffee at the hostel kitchen (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — leftover bread, cheese, and fruit (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Grab a budget meal from a Twizel takeaway or cook at the holiday park kitchen (~$10-12 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Glacier viewpoint from Kea Point is stunning and often less crowded than Hooker Valley. Check weather forecasts — afternoon cloud often builds in the Mount Cook area. Twizel has a New World supermarket — good place to restock groceries.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Twizel to Queenstown (approximately 2.5 hours via SH8). Stop at the Lindis Pass viewpoint for free panoramic tussock landscape photos. Arrive in Queenstown by late morning. Check in to a budget hostel (Nomads, Base Backpackers, or YHA Queenstown ~$35-45 NZD per night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Queenstown on foot — walk the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2 hours return, 300m elevation gain) for sweeping views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. This is one of the best free activities in Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Queenstown waterfront promenade. Browse the lively town centre. Have dinner at a budget-friendly spot. Research bungee jumping options and book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy for tomorrow to secure the best online price.

meals.breakfast: Cook oats at Twizel holiday park before departure (~$2 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap burger or wrap from a Queenstown food court or supermarket deli (~$10-12 NZD)
meals.dinner: Fergburger is iconic but pricey — opt for a budget meal at a local food court or cook at the hostel (~$10-14 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bridge Bungy online tonight — AJ Hackett offers the world's first commercial bungy jump site at ~$175 NZD. Book in advance for best pricing. Queenstown is expensive — use the hostel kitchen as much as possible to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Kawarau Bridge (20 minutes from Queenstown) for the iconic bungee jumping experience — the world's first commercial bungy jump site over the Kawarau River gorge (43m drop, ~$175 NZD). Arrive early for your booked slot. Watch others jump while waiting and enjoy the spectacular gorge scenery. The experience is unforgettable and worth the budget splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Gibbston Valley wine route back toward Queenstown. Stop at the free Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge lookout. Back in Queenstown, take the free Queenstown Gardens walk along the lakeside peninsula — beautiful native trees and mountain views with no entry fee.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump with a budget dinner at the hostel or a cheap local eatery. Share stories with fellow travellers at the hostel common room. Plan tomorrow's Milford Sound day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early hostel kitchen breakfast — toast, eggs, and coffee (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to take to Kawarau — sandwiches and snacks from supermarket (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a celebratory pasta dinner at the hostel kitchen (~$8 NZD) or treat yourself to a cheap pizza (~$15 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Kawarau Bridge at least 30 minutes before your booked jump time. Wear comfortable, secure clothing — no loose items. The jump video/photo package is extra (~$50 NZD) — decide in advance if you want it. Milford Sound day trip must be booked tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown at 7:00am for the drive to Milford Sound (approximately 4 hours via Te Anau). Stop at Mirror Lakes on the Milford Road (free, short 10-minute boardwalk) for iconic reflections of the Earl Mountains. Arrive at Milford Sound by 11:30am.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget Milford Sound cruise (Real Journeys or Go Orange offer competitive rates ~$65-80 NZD for a 2-hour cruise). See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls up close. Keep an eye out for dolphins, seals, and penguins. The scenery is among the most dramatic in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back to Queenstown, stopping at Te Anau for a cheap dinner. Arrive back in Queenstown by 9:00pm. Rest well — big day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Very early hostel kitchen breakfast before 7:00am departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirror Lakes or on the cruise (~$6-8 NZD from supermarket)
meals.dinner: Cheap meal at a Te Anau café or takeaway on the drive back (~$12-15 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's most scenic drives — allow extra time for stops. Book the cruise in advance online for best pricing. Bring rain gear — Milford Sound receives over 7 metres of rain annually. The drive is long but incredibly rewarding. Check road conditions before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the long Milford Sound day. Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed hostel breakfast. Head to Queenstown's Frankton Arm for a free morning walk along the lake trail (3km flat path with mountain views). Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market at Earnslaw Park if it's running for cheap local produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Arrowtown (20 minutes from Queenstown, free entry). Explore this beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush town on foot — the main street is charming and free to wander. Walk the free Arrow River Bridges Track (2 hours return) along the river through willows and historic Chinese settlement ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for the evening. Cook dinner at the hostel. Browse the lakefront for free evening entertainment — street performers often appear near the waterfront in November.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — scrambled eggs and toast (~$3-4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Cheap pie or sandwich from an Arrowtown bakery (~$6-8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a stir-fry at the hostel kitchen using supermarket vegetables (~$8-10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is free to explore and highly recommended. The Chinese Settlement ruins are historically significant and free to visit. Queenstown's supermarket (Countdown/Woolworths) is the most affordable place to stock up on groceries for hostel cooking.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Wanaka (1 hour via Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in NZ with spectacular views). Stop at the Crown Range Summit viewpoint for free panoramic photos. Arrive in Wanaka by 10:00am. Check in to a budget hostel (Wanaka Backpacker ~$30-40 NZD per night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roy's Peak Track (16km return, 1200m elevation gain, free) — one of New Zealand's most iconic ridge walks with jaw-dropping views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Start by 1:00pm — allow 5-6 hours. The summit views are extraordinary on a clear November day.
day_by_day.evening: Descend Roy's Peak by early evening. Soak tired legs in Lake Wanaka (free — the lake is refreshingly cold but beautiful). Cook dinner at the hostel. Visit the free That Wanaka Tree viewpoint at dusk for the famous lone willow tree photo.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and muffin from a Queenstown café before departing (~$6 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Roy's Peak — energy bars, sandwiches, and lots of water (~$6 NZD from supermarket)
meals.dinner: Cook a hearty recovery meal at the hostel — rice, beans, and vegetables (~$8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a strenuous hike — start early and bring 2-3L of water, sunscreen, and layers. The track is exposed with no shade. The That Wanaka Tree is a 5-minute walk from the town centre and best photographed at golden hour. Book hostel in advance for November.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wanaka town in the morning. Visit the free Wanaka lakefront and walk the Lake Wanaka Track (3km lakeside path, free). Pop into the Puzzling World attraction foyer for a free look (full entry ~$20 NZD — optional). Browse the local shops and grab a cheap coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Walk near Wanaka (20 minutes, free parking, free trail). This 2.5-hour loop offers stunning views of the Wanaka basin, Lake Hawea, and Mount Aspiring. A hidden gem that's far less crowded than Roy's Peak.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Christchurch direction or stay another night in Wanaka. Cook dinner at the hostel. Pack bags for the journey north tomorrow. Reflect on the incredible South Island experiences so far.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — porridge with honey and banana (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap sandwich from a Wanaka supermarket deli (~$6-8 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple but filling meal at the hostel — pasta bake with canned tuna (~$7-9 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Lake walk is free and highly recommended — far fewer crowds than Roy's Peak with equally impressive views. Stock up on groceries in Wanaka before heading north as options become limited. Check weather for the drive back toward Christchurch.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Wanaka early and drive north toward the West Coast via the Haast Pass (SH6). Stop at the free Thunder Creek Falls (10-minute walk from the road) and Blue Pools Walk (1 hour return, free) near Makarora — stunning turquoise glacier-fed pools in beech forest. Arrive at the West Coast by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Franz Josef or Fox Glacier village (depending on driving pace). Take the free self-guided glacier valley walk to the Fox Glacier terminal face viewpoint (2 hours return, free). The dramatic ice face and moraine landscape are awe-inspiring even from the valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Find budget accommodation at a Fox Glacier holiday park or hostel (~$25-35 NZD). Cook dinner at the campsite kitchen. Star gaze from the campsite — the West Coast has minimal light pollution and November skies can be spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Early hostel kitchen breakfast in Wanaka before departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Blue Pools or Thunder Creek Falls (~$6 NZD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the campsite kitchen using remaining groceries (~$8-10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is one of NZ's most scenic — allow plenty of time for stops. Blue Pools can be crowded by midday — arrive early. Glacier access is free from the valley floor. Helicopter glacier walks are available but expensive (~$200+ NZD). Check DOC website for current glacier access conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final day — drive from the West Coast back to Christchurch via Arthur's Pass (approximately 4 hours). Stop at Arthur's Pass National Park for a short free walk — the Devils Punchbowl Waterfall Track (1 hour return) leads to a stunning 131m waterfall. Look for kea (alpine parrots) in the village — they are cheeky and entertaining.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Christchurch. Arrive by early afternoon. Return rental car if applicable. Head back to Aegean Bliss Resort to collect any stored luggage. Spend the final afternoon exploring the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free entry) — a beautiful 21-hectare garden in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Christchurch — treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget meal to celebrate the end of an incredible 13-day South Island adventure. Visit the Christchurch Night Market if timing aligns for cheap diverse food options. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Campsite kitchen breakfast before early departure (~$3 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab food in Arthur's Pass village — the café does reasonable pies (~$8-10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Christchurch Night Market food stalls (~$10-15 NZD) or a sit-down budget meal at a local restaurant to celebrate the trip (~$18-22 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank — petrol stations in Arthur's Pass are expensive, fill up in Springfield instead. The Christchurch Botanic Gardens are free and a wonderful final afternoon activity. Check flight departure time and allow 2 hours for airport check-in. The Arthur's Pass road can be foggy in the morning — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch Airport, collect luggage and rental car, then drive to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented. Explore the immediate surroundings and enjoy the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center for a relaxed first evening. Explore the local waterfront area, browse shops, and unwind after the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Airport café or a quick bite at a casual eatery near the resort — try a classic NZ meat pie or fish and chips
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant near the resort — look for fresh local seafood such as green-lipped mussels or blue cod, budget around NZD $35–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pick up your rental car at the airport — essential for South Island travel. Purchase a NZ SIM card and download offline maps. Stock up on snacks and water at a nearby supermarket. Rest well as big adventures begin tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools — soak in the natural geothermal mineral pools surrounded by the Southern Alps. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to enjoy the pools before crowds build up. Choose from various temperature pools and enjoy the mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the thermal soak, lace up your hiking boots for the Hanmer Forest Hike. Explore the well-marked trails through the pine and beech forest, with options ranging from the easy Woodland Walk (1 hour) to the more challenging Conical Hill Track (2–3 hours) with panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort area. Stop at a local pub or casual restaurant in Hanmer Springs village before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort or a café near the resort before departing — eggs on toast or a smoothie bowl, NZD $15–25
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab a sandwich and coffee from a café in Hanmer Springs village — budget NZD $15–20
meals.dinner: Dine at The Hanmer Springs Tavern or Powerhouse Café in Hanmer Springs village — hearty NZ lamb burger or pasta, NZD $30–45 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanmer Springs entry fees apply — adult pool entry is approximately NZD $30. Book online in advance to save time. Bring a towel, swimwear, and sunscreen. The drive from the resort area is approximately 1.5–2 hours depending on your exact base location.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the scenic drive south toward Queenstown via the stunning Mackenzie Basin and Lake Tekapo. Stop at Lake Tekapo to photograph the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd and the brilliant turquoise glacial lake. Short lakeside walk (30–45 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Lake Pukaki for breathtaking views of Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in the milky-blue waters. Stop at the Lake Pukaki viewpoint and enjoy the scenic picnic area. Continue to your overnight stop in Twizel or Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Queenstown — check into accommodation. Take an evening stroll along the Queenstown waterfront along Lake Wakatipu and explore the vibrant town center.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — continental spread or eggs, NZD $15–20
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Pukaki — pick up fresh supplies from a bakery or supermarket in Twizel, NZD $15
meals.dinner: Dinner in Queenstown at a mid-range restaurant — try Fergburger (iconic NZ burger institution) or Rata restaurant for local cuisine, NZD $25–45 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is primarily a travel day — approximately 5–6 hours of driving total with stops. Fill up on fuel before leaving the resort area. The drive through the Mackenzie Basin is one of the most scenic in New Zealand — allow extra time for photo stops. Book Queenstown accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3 hours from Queenstown or 1 hour if staying in Twizel). Begin the Hooker Valley Track — a spectacular 10km return trail crossing three swing bridges over glacial streams with direct views of Aoraki/Mount Cook at 3,724m.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Hooker Valley Track, reaching the Hooker Lake terminal glacier viewpoint. Enjoy lunch at the trail end with stunning mountain views. On the return walk, take time to spot alpine plants and listen for kea (alpine parrots). Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre at The Hermitage.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown. Rest your legs and enjoy a quiet evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown or Twizel before the drive — café eggs benedict or porridge, NZD $18–25
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from Queenstown — sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Queenstown dinner at a mid-range spot — try The Cow (cozy pizza and pasta restaurant) or Bespoke Kitchen for wholesome options, NZD $30–45 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is rated easy-moderate and takes approximately 3 hours return. No booking required. Wear layers as mountain weather changes rapidly. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a rain jacket. November is late spring in NZ — wildflowers may be in bloom along the track.

day_by_day.morning: The big one — Nevis Bungy Jump! Head to the AJ Hackett Nevis Bungy base in Queenstown town center for your briefing and transfer. Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. The 8.5-second freefall reaches speeds of up to 150 km/h.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a scenic gondola ride up Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. Optionally try the luge tracks at the top for more thrills at a lower intensity. Browse the Skyline complex and enjoy the views.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump with a special dinner out in Queenstown. Explore the lively Queenstown nightlife if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the jump — don't eat too heavily beforehand. Try a smoothie and toast at a café, NZD $12–18
meals.lunch: Post-jump celebration lunch at a Queenstown lakefront café — burgers, salads, or wraps, NZD $20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Amisfield Bistro or Rata — modern NZ cuisine with local wine, NZD $45–65 per person as a treat

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy well in advance — it costs approximately NZD $275 per person. Weight limits apply (45–127 kg). A video and photo package is available for an additional fee — worth purchasing to capture the moment. The gondola costs approximately NZD $36 return. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and closed-toe shoes for the bungy.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery day — take a scenic morning hike on the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3 hours return, moderate). The trail winds through pine forest to the summit at 907m, offering 360-degree views of the Remarkables, Lake Wakatipu, and Cecil Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a relaxed afternoon stroll along the lake peninsula. Explore the rose gardens, frisbee golf course, and lakeside paths. Alternatively, take a short cruise on the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship across Lake Wakatipu (approximately 1 hour).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant restaurant and bar scene. Visit the Queenstown Night Market (held on Fridays) if timing aligns, or enjoy drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a Queenstown café before the hike — avocado toast or a full NZ breakfast, NZD $20–28
meals.lunch: Lakeside café lunch or food truck in Queenstown Gardens area — fish tacos or gourmet sandwiches, NZD $18–25
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Vudu Café & Larder or Winnies Gourmet Pizza Bar — relaxed atmosphere, NZD $25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: This day allows your body to recover from the bungy jump while still staying active. The Queenstown Hill hike is free and well-signposted. TSS Earnslaw cruise costs approximately NZD $55 per person. Queenstown Night Market runs on Fridays year-round along the waterfront.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours from Queenstown) — the gateway to Fiordland National Park and the start of the Routeburn Track. Check into Te Anau accommodation and visit the Department of Conservation (DOC) visitor center to get trail information and conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and Lake Te Anau shoreline. Take a short afternoon walk on the Kepler Track Day Walk along the lakeshore (2–3 hours return, easy). Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves for a magical underground boat tour.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and early to bed — a big hiking day begins tomorrow. Prepare your pack, check gear, and review the Routeburn Track plan.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Queenstown before departing — café stop, NZD $18–25
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Te Anau café upon arrival — try The Fat Duck or Sandfly Café for local favorites, NZD $18–25
meals.dinner: Dinner at Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — known for game meats and local produce, NZD $35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves in advance — tours cost approximately NZD $55 per person and run multiple times daily. Stock up on trail food and supplies at the Te Anau supermarket for the Routeburn Track days. The Routeburn Track Great Walk requires DOC hut bookings — confirm these well in advance as they sell out months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to the Routeburn Track Divide trailhead (approximately 1.5 hours drive from Te Anau, or arrange a shuttle). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track — one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks. Start from The Divide and hike to Lake Howden Hut (approximately 1 hour, easy warm-up section through beech forest).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Lake Howden Hut past the Earland Falls viewpoint (stunning 174m waterfall) and through subalpine tussock to Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4–5 hours total from The Divide). Arrive at the hut, settle in, and explore the area around the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the hut experience — cook dinner using your packed supplies, meet fellow trampers from around the world, and watch the sunset over the alpine landscape from Routeburn Falls.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation in Te Anau before shuttle departure — packed or café, NZD $15–20
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, cheese, crackers, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at Routeburn Falls Hut using packed supplies — freeze-dried hiking meal or pasta with pre-cooked ingredients

day_by_day.notes: DOC hut booking is mandatory and costs approximately NZD $65 per person per night. Routeburn Falls Hut has 48 bunks, cooking facilities, and flush toilets. Pack a lightweight sleeping bag liner. November weather can include rain — a quality waterproof jacket is essential. The track is approximately 32km total over 2–4 days.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the most spectacular section of the Routeburn Track — hike from Routeburn Falls Hut up to the Harris Saddle (1,255m) through open alpine terrain with sweeping views. This section is the highlight of the entire track with panoramic vistas of Fiordland and Mt Aspiring National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Harris Saddle along the exposed ridge to Routeburn Flats Hut or Lake Mackenzie Hut (depending on fitness and pace). The route traverses dramatic alpine terrain with views in every direction. Lake Mackenzie Hut sits above a pristine glacial lake — one of the most beautiful hut locations in NZ.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Lake Mackenzie Hut. Take a short walk down to the lake shore for an optional swim in the crystal-clear glacial water (brave souls only — very cold!). Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge or muesli cooked at Routeburn Falls Hut — pack oats and dried fruit
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten at Harris Saddle — energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, and a wrap
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dinner at Lake Mackenzie Hut — hearty freeze-dried meal or instant noodles with added protein

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section is exposed to alpine weather — check conditions the evening before with hut wardens. The optional side trip to Conical Hill from Harris Saddle adds 45 minutes but offers extraordinary 360-degree views. Distance for this day is approximately 11–14km depending on your pace and stops.

day_by_day.morning: Final day on the Routeburn Track — hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut down through ancient beech forest to the Routeburn Shelter at the Queenstown end (approximately 4–5 hours, 10km). The descent through towering beech trees draped in moss is magical. Cross the swing bridges over the Routeburn River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shuttle or drive back to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour). Check back into Queenstown accommodation. Enjoy a long, hot shower and rest your legs. Treat yourself to a massage or spa treatment at one of Queenstown's wellness centers.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track Great Walk — a genuine achievement worth celebrating!

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast cooked at Lake Mackenzie Hut — instant oats and coffee before the final descent
meals.lunch: Finish remaining trail snacks on the walk, then grab a well-earned burger or café meal in Glenorchy or Queenstown upon finishing
meals.dinner: Special completion dinner at Botswana Butchery or Bazaar International Buffet in Queenstown — treat yourself, NZD $45–70 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your shuttle from the Routeburn Shelter back to Queenstown — operators include Info & Track (approximately NZD $55 per person). The track exit is at the Routeburn Shelter on the Glenorchy-Queenstown Road. A massage at a Queenstown spa costs approximately NZD $80–120 for 60 minutes and is highly recommended after 3 days of hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Milford Sound (approximately 4 hours via Te Anau). The drive itself is one of the world's great road journeys — stop at the Mirror Lakes, Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain, and the Homer Tunnel. Arrive in time for the Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo — paddle through the majestic fiord surrounded by Mitre Peak (1,692m), cascading waterfalls including Lady Bowen Falls and Stirling Falls, and the chance to paddle directly under the falls. The combo includes a guided coastal hike through ancient rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Te Anau (approximately 2 hours). Overnight in Te Anau. Reflect on the extraordinary day in one of New Zealand's most iconic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown before the long drive — grab a takeaway coffee and pastry, NZD $10–15
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at one of the scenic stops on the Milford Road — Mirror Lakes or the Eglinton Valley
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Te Anau restaurant — try The Sandfly Café or Ristorante Pizzeria Paradiso for relaxed evening dining, NZD $25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo costs approximately NZD $195–225 per person — book well in advance as it is extremely popular. Depart Queenstown by 7:00 AM to allow time for scenic stops. The Homer Tunnel is a one-lane tunnel — traffic is controlled by lights. Milford Sound receives very high rainfall — a waterproof jacket is essential but rain actually enhances the waterfall experience.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau back north toward Christchurch — a long scenic drive. Stop at Lake Tekapo again for a morning walk around the Church of the Good Shepherd and along the lake shore. The light in the morning is exceptional for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north. Stop at Geraldine township for lunch and a browse of the local artisan shops and galleries. Visit the Talbot Forest Cheese shop for local NZ cheese tasting. Continue toward Christchurch.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Christchurch. Explore the revitalized city center — visit the Cardboard Cathedral, the Botanic Gardens, and the vibrant Re:START Mall area. Enjoy a final evening in the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Te Anau café before departing — eggs on toast or a smoothie bowl, NZD $18–25
meals.lunch: Lunch in Geraldine at a local café — homemade pies, soups, and artisan breads, NZD $15–22
meals.dinner: Dinner in Christchurch at a mid-range restaurant — try Hello Sunday or Gatherings for modern NZ cuisine, NZD $35–50 per person

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Christchurch is approximately 5.5–6 hours without stops. Consider breaking the journey into two days if energy is low after the intense hiking week. Christchurch has undergone remarkable regeneration since the 2011 earthquake — the city has a vibrant, creative energy worth exploring. Book Christchurch accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand — visit the Christchurch Botanic Gardens for a peaceful morning walk (free entry, 75 acres of beautiful gardens along the Avon River). Visit the Canterbury Museum (free entry) to learn about the South Island's natural and cultural history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Christchurch Airport. Return the rental car (allow 1–2 hours before your flight for car return and check-in). Final browse of duty-free shops — pick up NZ Manuka honey, Whittaker's chocolate, or merino wool souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure featuring world-class hiking, the world's highest bungy jump, kayaking in Milford Sound, and the beauty of Aoraki/Mount Cook.

meals.breakfast: Final NZ breakfast at a Christchurch café near the Botanic Gardens — full cooked breakfast or eggs benedict, NZD $20–28
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick café stop before check-in — NZD $15–20
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for car return, check-in, and security. Christchurch Airport has good dining and shopping options airside. Declare any food items to biosecurity — NZ has strict biosecurity laws. Ensure rental car is returned with a full tank of fuel to avoid surcharges. Download your photos and back up your memories before departure!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, traversing stunning alpine terrain between Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacial lakes, and ancient beech forests. A multi-day hike offering some of the most spectacular scenery in the Southern Hemisphere.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk this iconic 10km return trail through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, crossing swing bridges over glacial rivers with jaw-dropping views of New Zealand's highest peak. The trail ends at the stunning Hooker Glacier Lake filled with floating icebergs. A relatively accessible yet awe-inspiring alpine hike.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord surrounded by towering peaks and cascading waterfalls, then hike a section of the famous Milford Track through ancient rainforest. Spot dolphins, seals, and penguins in their natural habitat. A guided full-day experience combining two of Fiordland's best adventures.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Forest Hike
experiences.description: Soak in natural geothermal mineral pools surrounded by the Southern Alps, then explore the Hanmer Forest Park trails through fragrant pine forests with panoramic mountain views. The combination of restorative hot pools and scenic hiking makes this a perfect recovery day experience for active travellers.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome champagne amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach to decompress from the flight and soak in your first views of the South Island coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Orientation dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring South Island seafood — Bluff oysters, crayfish, and Canterbury lamb — paired with Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: Light welcome platter arranged by the resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in confirmation in advance. Ask the concierge to brief you on the full 13-day itinerary and arrange any gear rentals or permits needed for upcoming activities.

day_by_day.morning: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Forest Hike — Begin with a guided forest hike through the Hanmer Forest Park, exploring native beech and pine trails with panoramic Southern Alps views. Your private guide will tailor the pace and route to your fitness level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools for a private mineral pool session. Indulge in a couples' or solo spa treatment — hot stone massage or alpine mud wrap — at a premium day spa adjacent to the pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private transfer. Dine at a local fine-dining restaurant in Hanmer Springs village before heading back, or opt for in-resort dining with a locally sourced à la carte menu.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic hamper prepared by the resort, enjoyed trailside with mountain views
meals.dinner: Monteith's Restaurant, Hanmer Springs — premium New Zealand beef and venison menu with South Island wine list

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking boots and layers. The thermal pools are clothing-required — pack a swimsuit. Pre-book the spa treatment to secure your preferred time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight from the resort area to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park — one of the most dramatic arrivals possible. Land near the Hooker Valley trailhead and begin the iconic Hooker Valley Track, crossing three swing bridges with Aoraki towering ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the 10km return Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier and the glacial terminal lake. Witness stunning turquoise icebergs calving from the glacier face. Return to the trailhead and enjoy a private gourmet picnic arranged by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Helicopter return to the resort area. Unwind with a sunset cocktail on your private balcony overlooking the beachfront. Dinner at the resort's oceanfront terrace.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your suite — continental spread with fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Luxury trailside picnic hamper: artisan cheeses, charcuterie, sourdough, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort oceanfront terrace — grilled South Island salmon, roasted root vegetables, and Central Otago Pinot Gris

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight is weather-dependent — the concierge should have a backup road transfer plan ready. Dress in warm, windproof layers as temperatures near the glacier are significantly cooler. Bring sunscreen and sunglasses — UV is intense at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy a late breakfast and a private yoga or stretch session on the beach, arranged through the resort's wellness concierge. Use this time to recharge before the more intensive days ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided kayak tour along the local coastline — explore sea caves, marine wildlife, and hidden coves inaccessible by foot. Premium single or double sea kayaks with a certified guide included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine tasting experience at a nearby boutique winery — private cellar tour and vertical tasting of estate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, hosted by the winemaker. Return to the resort for a light supper.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — full hot menu with freshly baked pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort's casual bar: fish tacos, prawn skewers, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private winery supper — antipasto boards and cheese platters paired with estate wines, followed by resort nightcap

day_by_day.notes: Confirm kayak tour weather conditions the evening prior. The winery visit is typically 2 hours — book the earliest evening slot to catch sunset over the vines.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Queenstown — the adventure capital of New Zealand. Check into a luxury Queenstown hotel for a two-night stay (arrange with concierge for a premium property such as Eichardt's Private Hotel or Matakauri Lodge). Morning arrival allows time to explore the Queenstown waterfront and Steamer Wharf precinct.
day_by_day.afternoon: NEVIS BUNGY JUMP — Take on New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A private shuttle transfers you to the Nevis site. After the jump, celebrate with a post-jump champagne toast arranged by the operator.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown fine dining — book a table at Amisfield Winery & Bistro or Rata Restaurant (Josh Emett's flagship). Celebrate the day's adrenaline with a world-class multi-course dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast at Aegean Bliss before departure — eggs your way, fresh fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Pre-jump lunch at Queenstown's Botswana Butchery — premium burger or salad to fuel the adventure
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — seasonal New Zealand tasting menu with matched wines

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy has a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, close-fitting clothing. The jump is weather-dependent but rarely cancelled. Book the jump for early-to-mid afternoon to allow time to settle in Queenstown first. Store valuables securely before jumping.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise hike up Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown — a challenging but spectacular 3–4 hour ascent rewarded with 360-degree panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Private guide included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and return to Queenstown by mid-afternoon. Indulge in a premium recovery spa treatment at your hotel — deep tissue massage or hydrotherapy soak. Optional: browse Queenstown's boutique shopping on the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a chartered vessel — canapés and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc served on deck as the sun sets behind The Remarkables. Dinner at Eichardt's Bar or a private in-suite dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the hotel — high-protein spread: eggs, avocado, smoked salmon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike recovery lunch at Queenstown's Sherwood Restaurant — wholesome, locally sourced seasonal menu
meals.dinner: Eichardt's Private Hotel dining room — intimate à la carte dinner with lake views and curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a strenuous hike — poles are recommended and available from the guide. Start by 6:00am to catch sunrise at the summit. Weather can change rapidly; your guide will assess conditions. The sunset cruise is approximately 2 hours — dress warmly as lake breezes are cool in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Queenstown to Te Anau — gateway to Fiordland National Park (approximately 2.5 hours). Check in to a premium Te Anau lodge (such as Fiordland Lodge). Morning arrival allows a lakeside walk along the Te Anau waterfront to stretch after the drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk through the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a private after-hours or small-group premium experience through the cave system, culminating in a silent boat ride through chambers filled with thousands of glowworms reflecting off the underground river.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the lodge with panoramic Fiordland mountain views. Enjoy a curated South Island game and seafood menu — venison, blue cod, and Southland cheese board — beside a log fire.

meals.breakfast: Queenstown hotel checkout breakfast — full hot buffet with made-to-order eggs
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed en route or lakeside in Te Anau — artisan sandwiches, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge dining room — 4-course dinner with Fiordland venison and Central Otago wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The glowworm caves are a UNESCO World Heritage site — follow all guide instructions regarding silence and no photography in the cave chambers. Book the premium private cave experience well in advance as it sells out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1 of a 2-day guided premium experience. Begin at the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Hike through ancient beech forest, crossing crystal-clear mountain streams toward the Routeburn Flats hut and beyond to the Falls Hut area. Private licensed guide accompanies throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue ascending through alpine meadows above the treeline with expansive views of Fiordland peaks. Reach the Lake Mackenzie area — one of the most scenic spots on the entire track. Arrive at premium lodge-style hut accommodation for overnight stay.
day_by_day.evening: Guided naturalist talk at the hut on Fiordland's ecology and geology. Communal but premium dinner prepared by the hut chef — hearty mountain cuisine with New Zealand wines. Stargazing session in one of the Southern Hemisphere's darkest sky zones.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure — porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Trailside lunch from packed gourmet hamper — wraps, trail mix, energy bars, and fruit
meals.dinner: Routeburn Track premium hut dinner — roast lamb, roasted vegetables, and dessert with wine

day_by_day.notes: Pack only essentials in a daypack — a porter service can be arranged through your premium guided operator to carry heavier gear between huts. Wear broken-in hiking boots. Layering is essential as alpine conditions can shift rapidly. The track is one of New Zealand's Great Walks and requires a Great Walk pass — your guide will have arranged this.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 2. Rise early for sunrise over Lake Mackenzie. Begin the day's hike ascending to Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the high point of the track with sweeping views across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains. Optional side trip to Conical Hill for even more panoramic vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the Hollyford Valley side of the track, passing through dramatic hanging valleys and waterfalls. Complete the track at the Divide shelter. Private vehicle transfer back to Te Anau lodge for a hot shower and well-deserved rest.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at Te Anau's finest restaurant — Sandfly Café or a private lodge dinner. Reflect on two days of world-class hiking over a premium New Zealand wine and seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot hut breakfast — scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, and fresh coffee at sunrise
meals.lunch: Final trailside lunch with remaining hamper provisions, enjoyed at Harris Saddle with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge — special celebration dinner: Bluff oysters, blue cod, and Southland berry pavlova

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be extremely windy and cold — pack a warm hat, gloves, and a windproof shell even in November. The descent to the Divide is approximately 4 hours. Confirm vehicle pickup time with your guide the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Te Anau lodge. Enjoy a long breakfast, a lodge spa treatment, and a gentle lakeside walk. This is intentionally a lighter day after two days of alpine hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo — Private transfer to Milford Sound (approximately 2 hours through the stunning Milford Road). Begin with a guided sea kayak on the fiord, paddling beneath Mitre Peak and past Stirling and Bowen Falls. Spray from the waterfalls is a highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight cruise option on Milford Sound — board a premium small-vessel overnight cruise (such as Fiordland Navigator) for a sunset dinner cruise into the deeper fiord. Watch for dolphins, fur seals, and rare Fiordland crested penguins.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely lodge breakfast — full spread with fresh pastries, fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed at Milford Sound before kayaking — smoked salmon bagels and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Fiordland Navigator overnight cruise dinner — 3-course buffet with New Zealand wines served as the fiord glows at dusk

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound receives extremely high rainfall — even on rainy days the fiord is spectacular with hundreds of temporary waterfalls. Waterproof gear is provided for kayaking. The overnight cruise is highly recommended — book well in advance as premium cabins are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up on the Milford Sound overnight cruise vessel anchored in the deep fiord. Early morning wildlife watching — dolphins are frequently seen at dawn. Enjoy a hot breakfast on board as the crew navigates back toward the Milford wharf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and take the scenic Milford Road back toward Te Anau, stopping at the Mirror Lakes and Eglinton Valley viewpoints for photography. Return to Te Anau lodge for checkout and private transfer back toward the resort area or onward to Wanaka for the next leg.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a premium Wanaka property (such as Minaret Station Alpine Lodge or Lakeside Apartments). Sunset dinner at Wanaka's finest restaurant — Francesca's Italian Kitchen or Ritual Café — overlooking Lake Wanaka.

meals.breakfast: Overnight cruise hot breakfast — eggs, bacon, toast, and fresh juice served on deck
meals.lunch: Casual lakeside lunch in Wanaka — gourmet pizza or fresh salads at a waterfront café
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — handmade pasta, wood-fired dishes, and premium Italian and NZ wine list

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Milford Sound to Wanaka via Te Anau is approximately 4–5 hours — arrange a comfortable private vehicle with a knowledgeable driver-guide who can narrate the landscape. Wanaka is a beautiful, quieter alternative to Queenstown and an ideal base for the final days.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise hike to Roys Peak above Lake Wanaka — a 16km return trail with one of New Zealand's most photographed viewpoints. Start at 5:30am to reach the summit for sunrise. The iconic view of the lake and Mount Aspiring is breathtaking in the early morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and return to Wanaka by midday. Enjoy a premium recovery lunch and an afternoon at leisure — optional visit to Puzzling World, a lakeside paddle board session, or a private wine tasting at Rippon Vineyard, one of New Zealand's most scenic wineries set directly above Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Rippon Vineyard's private dining experience or a chef's table reservation at a Wanaka fine dining venue. Celebrate the journey with a premium degustation menu and matched wines.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike early breakfast at the lodge — high-energy: oats, eggs, banana, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike brunch at Wanaka's Kika restaurant — shared plates, fresh local produce, and craft coffee
meals.dinner: Rippon Vineyard private dining or Wanaka's premier chef's table — 6-course degustation with estate wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is a strenuous 5–6 hour hike — an early start is essential both for the sunrise experience and to avoid the midday crowds. Poles are highly recommended. This is November, so daylight begins around 5:30am — perfect timing. Confirm Rippon Vineyard private dining well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Wanaka — leisurely lakeside breakfast and a gentle walk along the Lake Wanaka waterfront. Visit the famous lone willow tree in the lake for a final iconic South Island photograph. Browse local boutiques for premium New Zealand souvenirs — Merino wool, Manuka honey, and local art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Queenstown Airport or Wanaka Airport for departure flight. Allow ample time for check-in and baggage. Enjoy a final glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir in the airport lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days across the South Island — from thermal pools to glacier lakes, from 134-meter bungy jumps to the ancient silence of Milford Sound.

meals.breakfast: Final South Island breakfast at a Wanaka lakeside café — avocado toast, poached eggs, and flat white coffee
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge lunch or a farewell meal at a Wanaka café before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at departure destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for the transfer and airport formalities. Arrange luggage collection and resort checkout the evening prior to streamline the final morning. Consider sending any oversized gear (hiking poles, purchased items) ahead via courier to avoid excess baggage fees.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
